tool_input.command:
mkdir -p doc/adr && cd doc/adr && cat > 0001-record-architecture-decisions.md <<'EOF'
# 1. Record architecture decisions

Date: 2026-11-22

## Status

Accepted

## Context

We need to record the architectural decisions made on this project.

## Decision

We will use Architecture Decision Records, as [described by Michael Nygard](http://thinkrelevance.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions).

## Consequences

See Michael Nygard's article, linked above. For a lightweight ADR toolset, see Nat Pryce's [adr-tools](https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools).
EOF
cat > 0002-use-iso-8601-utc-strings-for-public-api-timestamps.md <<'EOF'
# 2. Use ISO 8601 UTC strings for public API timestamps

Date: 2026-11-22

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Our public API has represented timestamps as unix epoch integers. Client integrations have repeatedly run into timezone bugs when handling these values. Epoch integers are also unreadable in logs.

## Decision

We will represent all timestamps in our public API as ISO 8601 strings in UTC instead of unix epoch integers.

## Consequences

Timestamps become readable in logs, and the timezone bugs that epoch integers caused in client integrations should no longer occur.

Clients now have to parse strings into their own date-time types rather than consuming integers directly.

Payloads get slightly bigger, because a timestamp string takes more bytes than an integer.
EOF
ls
